steps.title: Give each tool one job
steps.content:
Dojofoo provides the course and learning interface. uv manages the Python interpreter, virtual environment, dependencies, and commands inside the Python project. Keeping those responsibilities separate makes the workspace reproducible without making an interactive course depend on Python merely to display a lesson.

You need Node.js to run the dojofoo CLI. For Python work, this lesson uses uv to acquire Python rather than relying on whichever interpreter happens to be installed globally.

steps.title: Check the responsibility boundary
steps.prompt: Which tool in this setup installs and manages the Python version and Python dependencies?
steps.explanation: uv owns the Python environment. Dojofoo owns the course, local learning state, and teaching UI.

steps.title: Install uv
steps.content:
If you already use mise, install uv with:

mise use -g uv@latest

Otherwise, use uv's official installation instructions for your operating system at https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/. Then confirm the command is available:

uv --version

Using mise is convenient, but dojofoo does not require it for this lesson.

steps.title: Let uv install Python
steps.content:
Install a current Python release without modifying the operating system's Python:

uv python install 3.13

Confirm what uv can see:

uv python list

A project can later pin the interpreter with `uv python pin 3.13`, producing a portable `.python-version` file.

steps.title: Retrieve the command
steps.prompt: Which command asks uv to install Python 3.13?
steps.explanation: `uv python install 3.13` asks uv to acquire a compatible Python 3.13 release. It avoids coupling the project to the system interpreter.

steps.title: Create the Python workspace
steps.content:
From an empty project directory, initialize and pin the environment:

uv init
uv python pin 3.13
uv add --dev pytest

Run Python and tests through uv so the project environment is selected consistently:

uv run python --version
uv run pytest

The optional `examples/hello.py` shipped with this dojo is a tiny destination you can copy into your own project and run with `uv run python hello.py`.

steps.title: Initialize the dojo
steps.content:
In the same project directory, initialize dojofoo for the coding harness you use. For example:

npx dojofoo install --codex

Replace `--codex` with another supported harness flag when appropriate. Then install a course and open the local UI:

npx dojofoo add dojofoo/starter-interactive
npx dojofoo ui --open

The Python environment and dojofoo learning state now coexist in the project while remaining independently replaceable.

steps.title: Use the managed environment
steps.prompt: Which command runs pytest through the environment managed by uv?
steps.explanation: `uv run pytest` resolves the project environment before launching pytest, so the command does not depend on an activated shell or a global installation.

steps.title: You now have a reproducible baseline
steps.content:
The resulting workspace has three clear layers: uv manages Python, Git carries project configuration and learner-owned work, and dojofoo keeps local course/session state while presenting the lesson.

Use this repository as the baseline for authoring another interactive dojo: change the metadata in `dojo.json`, replace the lesson definition, and keep the package allowlist limited to material the learner actually needs.
